000
FXUS65 KPSR 100837
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
137 AM MST Sat Oct 10 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- An unsettled weather pattern will prevail throughout the weekend as
  the remnants of Tropical Cyclone Rachel move into the southwest
  United States, resulting in heightened chances for showers and 
  thunderstorms, widespread gusty winds on Sunday, and much cooler
  temperatures.

- Rain chances will continue for portions of the region, especially 
  across south-central AZ, early next week along with well-below 
  normal temperatures. 

- A drier and quieter weather pattern is expected by the middle
  and latter portion of next week along with gradually warming
  temperatures. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SUNDAY/... 
After a fairly benign weather pattern across the southwestern 
United States during the last week, big changes are coming for 
this upcoming weekend. Current water vapor satellite imagery as 
well as objective analysis show a large northern stream trough 
diving into the Pacific Northwest while Tropical Storm Rachel, 
being steered northeastward by another cutoff low is located 
several hundred miles to the south- southwest of San Diego. Rachel
will continue to migrate north- northeastward throughout the day,
making landfall along the far Northern Baja Peninsula by late 
tonight before accelerating north-northeastward through San Diego
and western Riverside Counties and towards the Mohave Desert 
during the day Sunday. 

South southwesterly flow will transport abundant moisture into 
the region throughout the day today, with the ensembles showing 
mean PWATs exceeding over 200-250% of normal by early this 
evening. The increasing moisture combined with the increasing jet 
dynamics from the west coast trough will support scattered showers
and storms to break out. Latest hi-res guidance shows activity, 
mostly in the form of elevated showers, developing over southwest 
AZ starting late morning with scattered showers and storms 
developing across portions of south-central AZ through southeast 
CA during the afternoon/early evening hours. Some gusty winds and 
brief heavy rainfall will be the main threats with any storms that
materialize as instability will be quite marginal with MUCAPE 
values at less than 500 J/KG. The chances for more robust 
convection will likely come late tonight into Sunday morning as 
better low-level moisture with the arrival of Rachel will support 
a window of higher instability upwards of 500-1000 J/KG of MUCAPE.
The higher instability combined with vertical wind shear in 
excess of 40 kts will support a severe threat, with SPC 
highlighting much of the area under a marginal risk. Damaging wind
gusts will be the main threat, however, with low-level shear 
increasing above 20 kts along with 0-3 km Storm Relative Helicity 
over 100-200 m2/s2, there will be a non-zero threat for a brief 
tornado or two. 

As the remnants of Rachel approach southern CA combined with height 
falls from the large scale trough to the west, low-level winds will 
be increasing with a belt of 850 mb upwards of 50 kts. This will 
support non-thunderstorm wind gusts exceeding 40 mph starting after 
midnight across southeast CA into southwest AZ before the stronger 
winds spread further east into south-central AZ by the early to mid-
morning hours Sunday. Wind gusts this high could certainty result in 
areas of blowing dust in the dust prone areas. As the remnants of 
Rachel move northward into southern Nevada by late Sunday 
afternoon/early evening, winds will weaken as the gradient weakens.

In terms of rainfall amounts, given that much of the activity will 
be mostly scattered in nature, amounts across much of the area will 
be under 0.75" with the potential that some areas see next to 
nothing. However, there can be some locally higher amounts in excess 
of 1" in areas that see a training of convection. The more favorable 
area for more widespread activity will be mainly across Joshua Tree 
National Park, close to where Rachel will track, and thus the 
potential will exist for more widespread amounts in excess of 1" 
with a Flood Watch in effect from this evening through Sunday 
afternoon.

After the couple of days of widespread highs in the triple digits, 
temperatures this weekend will steadily cool. Lower desert highs 
this afternoon will be about 10 degrees cooler compared to Friday 
with readings in the low to mid 90s. The more abundant cloud cover 
as well as rainfall activity will cause temperatures to cool another 
7-10 degrees on Sunday as afternoon highs only reach the low to 
middle 80s.

&&

.LONG TERM /MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/... 
Unsettled weather will continue through early next week as the large-
scale trough that will settle across the west coast over the weekend 
will gradually migrate eastward. The associated large-scale forcing 
for ascent combined with ample low-level moisture will support 
scattered showers and embedded thunderstorms during the day, mainly 
across the foothills and higher terrain areas north and east of 
Phoenix in upslope flow. Thereafter, as the main cold front 
associated with the trough moves through late Monday night into 
Tuesday morning, there will likely be a band of showers with 
embedded thunderstorms that moves through, particularly across south-
central AZ, before rain chances end by Tuesday afternoon/evening as 
drier air filters in. At this point any of the rain that falls early 
next week will generally be of the nuisance type. Quieter weather
with near zero rain chances can be expected starting Wednesday 
and will persist through the end of the week.

With the presence of the trough as well as more abundant cloud 
cover, well-below normal temperatures are expected during the first 
half of the week with many of the lower desert locations likely 
staying in the 70s for afternoon highs. Early morning lows will also 
be below normal with the coolest morning expected on Wednesday when 
many areas are expected to drop into the 50s with even some 40s 
across the higher terrain areas. Temperatures will then gradually 
rebound into the 80s by the latter portion of the week.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0540Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
The primary weather issues will be SHRA and potentially embedded 
TSRA entering the Phoenix metro Saturday afternoon and evening, and 
subsequent the effect on winds as midlevel cigs develop and lower. 
Confidence is good that E/SE winds will prevail through Saturday 
morning as 10-15K ft AGL cigs fill in across the area. Scattered 
SHRA should enter the western portions of the metro early Saturday 
afternoon, and may allow winds to shift to a W/SW direction. 
Coverage of SHRA appears low enough to preclude a predominant 
mention, and will advertise a prolonged period of VCSH. A few 
embedded TSRA will also be possible heading into the evening, but 
odds only justify a prob30 mention at this time with potentially 
erratic, gusty winds. Confidence is better that an east component 
will settle back into the area Saturday night, and have kept a VCSH 
mention though its more uncertain how expansive SHRA will be. 

Sunday outlook: High impact weather still appears to be arriving at 
all terminals Sunday mid/late morning through the afternoon. 
SHRA/TSRA should surge into the area with gusty south winds and 
MVFR/IFR cigs. The lower cigs and TSRA threat should be rather short 
lived over a 3-4 hour window late morning through early afternoon 
before lifting out of the aerodrome space. However, very strong S/SW 
winds will fill in behind the SHRA with gusts 30kt or higher 
throughout the afternoon. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
Periods of SHRA with the potential for isolated TSRA along with 
erratic wind directions will be the main weather issues as thick 
midlevel cigs develop over the area. Winds should become more 
variable in direction overnight, then obtaining an E/SE component 
Saturday. Scattered showers would most likely impact KBLH by early 
afternoon as 10K ft cigs cover the area. At this point, a VCSH 
adequately describes the coverage, though enough odds for TSRA exist 
at KBLH to include a prob30. Uncertainty in winds and weather grow 
significantly Saturday night and Sunday as a period of high impact 
weather moves into the region. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
A much more unsettled weather pattern will develop over the weekend 
as increasing moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical 
Storm Rachel brings increasing rain chances. The chances for 
showers and storms increase starting This afternoon/evening and 
continues into Sunday with a greater than 50-70% chance of wetting
rainfall area wide. Winds will also increase significantly, 
especially late tonight through Sunday with widespread gusts 
exceeding 30-40 mph. With the increasing moisture and cooler 
temperatures, MinRH values will increase from 25-40% today to 
45-70% on Sunday along with good to excellent overnight 
recoveries. Another weather system will bring additional chances 
for wetting rainfall early next week, mainly for the eastern 
districts, before quieter weather settles in by the middle of the 
week. Temperatures will steadily cool this weekend, with well-
below normal temperatures expected for the first half of the next
week. 

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Wind Advisory from 2 AM to 5 PM MST Sunday for AZZ530>533-535-
     536.

     Wind Advisory from 8 AM to 5 PM MST Sunday for AZZ534-537>563.

CA...Wind Advisory from 2 AM to 5 PM PDT Sunday for CAZ560>570.

     Flood Watch from this afternoon through Sunday afternoon for 
     CAZ560-561-568.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Lojero
LONG TERM...Lojero 
AVIATION...18 
FIRE WEATHER...Lojero
